question.text:
What will happen when the following code is compiled?

#include <stdio.h>

struct Point {
    int x;
    int y;
};

int main() {
    struct Point p1 = {2, 4};
    struct Point p2;

    p2 = p1;
    p2.x = 10;

    if (p1 == p2)
        printf("Same");
    else
        printf("%d %d", p1.x, p2.x);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{Same}$
     
  2. $\texttt{2 10}$
     
  3. $\texttt{10 10}$
     
  4. Compilation error
question.subject: Programming in C

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

struct Box {
    int width;
    int height;
};

int main() {
    struct Box b = {4, 6};
    struct Box *p = &b;

    p->width = p->width + 2;
    (*p).height = (*p).height + p->width;

    printf("%d %d", b.width, b.height);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{4 6}$
     
  2. $\texttt{6 10}$
     
  3. $\texttt{6 12}$
     
  4. Compilation error

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

struct Student {
    int roll;
    int marks;
};

int main() {
    struct Student s[3] = {
        {1, 70},
        {2, 80},
        {3, 90}
    };

    s[1].marks = s[1].marks + 5;
    s[2].roll = s[0].roll + s[1].roll;

    printf("%d %d %d", s[1].marks, s[2].roll, s[2].marks);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{80 3 90}$
     
  2. $\texttt{85 3 90}$
     
  3. $\texttt{85 2 90}$
     
  4. $\texttt{85 3 95}$

question.text:
What is the output of the following code?

#include <stdio.h>

struct Item {
    int code;
    int price;
};

void update(struct Item *p) {
    p->price = p->price + 20;
    (*p).code = (*p).code + 1;
}

int main() {
    struct Item i1 = {10, 100};

    update(&i1);

    printf("%d %d", i1.code, i1.price);

    return 0;
}
  1. $\texttt{10 100}$
     
  2. $\texttt{11 120}$
     
  3. $\texttt{10 120}$
     
  4. Compilation error
